question: A key appointment in India's disaster management sector was made in 2024. Which Indian Police Service (IPS) officer took charge as the "Director General of the National Disaster Response Force", leading the nation's primary disaster relief efforts?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Piyush Anand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Piyush Anand IPS officer Uttar Pradesh 1991 batch**, who is presently posted as Special DG CISF Ministry of Home Affairs Government of India, has been appointed as Director General, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)Ministry of Home Affairs Government of India, in place of Atul Karwal, IPS (GJ/88) upon his superannuation on 31.03.2024.
 
• The NDRF is India's premier agency for disaster management and plays a critical role in disaster relief and rescue operations across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atul Karwal**

 
 
• Appointed DG of NDRF on November 15, 2021, and served until March 31, 2024, when he retired.
 
• A decorated officer known for his leadership, ultra-marathon running, mountaineering (including Everest), and martial arts, he led NDRF through significant operations like Operation Dost. 
 
 
 
• **Rajeev Kapoor**
 
 
• Rajeev Kapoor is another prominent IPS officer but has not served as the Director General of the NDRF.
 
• His contributions lie in other areas of public service and law enforcement, unrelated to disaster management.
 
 
 
• **Pradeep Kumar**
 
 
• Pradeep Kumar is a senior government official but has no connection with the NDRF's leadership role or disaster management operations.
 
• His expertise lies in other administrative domains rather than emergency response or relief efforts.
 
 
 
• **About the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)**
 
 
• The NDRF was formed in 2006 under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, to respond to natural and man-made disasters.
 
• It comprises 12 battalions deployed across the country and is equipped with specialized training and modern equipment to handle disasters.
